questionText:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) On dilution, conductivity of all the electrolytes decreases.
(B) On dilution, the number of ions per unit volume decreases.
(C) Molar conductivity increases with dilution.
(D) Limiting molar conductivity is the conductivity at a very high concentration.
 
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed both statements were correct.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies that both statements contain factual errors.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Statement (A): Correct, conductivity of all electrolytes (strong and weak) decreases on dilution. Statement (B): Correct, number of ions per unit volume decreases on dilution. Statement (C): Correct, molar conductivity increases with dilution. Statement (D): Incorrect, limiting molar conductivity is at infinite dilution (zero concentration). Thus, (A), (B), and (C) only are correct.
Hence, option (B) is correct.

questionText: In the Hall-Héroult electrolytic extraction of aluminium from molten alumina ($Al_2O_3$), cryolite ($Na_3AlF_6$) and fluorspar ($CaF_2$) are added primarily to:

options.text: Act as reducing agents to convert $Al^{3+}$ directly into liquid aluminium
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Lower the melting point of alumina from $2323\text{ K}$ to around $1173\text{ K}$ and increase electrical conductivity
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Electrolysis of Molten Alumina Cryolite Role.

options.text: Form a protective gaseous shield of fluorine over the carbon anode

Lower the melting point of alumina from $2323\text{ K}$ to around $1173\text{ K}$ and increase electrical conductivity

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
